svg.text: Why is there such a shortage of family-friendly housing? Land-use and environmental regulations have a
lot to do with it. We hear how Austin has been rewriting the rules — and ask whether other cities could
do the same. (Part two of a two-part series.)
• Nick Bloom, professor of economics at Stanford University.
• Ed Glaeser, professor of economics at Harvard University.
• Kathy Hochul, governor of New York.
• Melissa Kearney, professor of economics at the University of Notre Dame.
• Lyman Stone, director of the Pronatalism Initiative at the Institute for Family Studies.
• Kirk Watson, mayor of Austin, Texas.
• "Austin’s Surge of New Housing Construction Drove Down Rents," by Liz Clifford, Seva Rodnyansky, and
• "Inequality, not regulation, drives America's housing affordability crisis," by Maximilian Buchholz,
Tom Kemeny, Gregory F. Randolph, and Michael Storper (International Inequalities Institute, 2026)
• "Zoning and the Dynamics of Urban Redevelopment," by Vincent Rollet (SSRN, 2025).
• "Can Housing Policy Raise Birth Rates? Lessons from Federal Mortgage Programs During the Baby Boom,"
by Lisa J. Dettling and Melissa Schettini Kearney (NBER, 2025)
• "The housing theory of everything," by John Myers, Sam Bowman, and Ben Southwood (Works in Progress,
• "House Prices and Birth Rates: The Impact of the Real Estate Market on the Decision to Have a Baby,"
Lisa J. Dettling and Melissa Schettini Kearney (NBER, 2011)
• "Why is Manhattan so Expensive? Regulation and the Rise in House Prices," by Edward Glaeser, Joseph
• "Why Aren't We Having More Babies?" by Freakonomics Radio (2025).
